---
title: "How it works"
---

## What the map shows

Each neighborhood (Census block group) is colored by the fastest
scheduled trip to Binghamton University's main campus: walking to a
nearby BC Transit stop, plus the bus ride.

**The four views:**

- **Groceries (Saturday):** the faster of walking straight to a
  supermarket (up to 800 m) or taking the bus to one, arriving by noon.
- **To campus, weekday:** arriving on campus by 8am on a Tuesday.
- **To campus, Saturday:** arriving by noon.
- **Leaving campus, weeknight:** leaving between 10 and 11pm. BC Transit's
  last bus off campus leaves at 8:31pm, so almost every neighborhood
  shows no access.

## Data

- **Bus schedules:** BC Transit's public GTFS feed (Broome County).
- **Neighborhoods:** U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey
  5-year estimates (2020–2024).
- **Supermarkets:** OpenStreetMap (`shop=supermarket`), spot-checked
  against store directories.
  
- **OCCT schedules** (night headline only): OCCT Fall 2026 schedule,
  checked October 2026. Not part of the map.

## Assumptions and limits

- Riders walk up to 800 m (about 11 minutes) to a stop, at 1.2 m/s.
- Each neighborhood is measured from one point inside it, so large
  rural areas are approximate.
- Times are based on schedules, not real-time bus locations.
- Some stop times are estimated between scheduled timepoints.
- **OCCT (the student bus system) is not included**, because its
  schedules aren't in BC Transit's data. Student neighborhoods are
  better connected than this map shows, especially late at night.
- Census numbers are survey estimates with margins of error.
